xep.header:
Multi-User eXchange (MUX) This specification defines a group communication service whose rooms hold a persistent membership, ordered roles with permission sets, and several channels. Every text channel is also a Multi-User Chat room, so existing clients take part without change. The document is a framework: it defines the entities, the addressing, discovery, creation, joining, permissions, invitations and the stamps the service puts on messages, and reuses existing extensions for everything else. &LEGALNOTICE; xxxx ProtoXEP Standards Track Standards Council

section1.p: &xep0045; gives XMPP one room with one list of occupants, where membership and presence are the same thing and a client must be joined to be told anything. &xep0369; separated the two but needed a change on every participant's home server, which few deployed. Meanwhile group communication elsewhere settled on a different shape: a place with a persistent membership and ordered roles, divided into channels, some of them text and some of them voice.

MUX (Multi-User eXchange) is that shape on XMPP, without asking anything of the home server. A MUX service hosts rooms. A room has members, who stay members while offline, hats (&xep0317;) that carry permission sets, and channels. A text channel is a complete Multi-User Chat room backed by the room's state, so any client that speaks &xep0045; can read and write in it today. What the room needs beyond that - creation, a join that is not a presence, subscriptions, a paged member list, permissions, invitation tokens - is a small set of IQs in one namespace, defined here. Everything else is an existing extension used as written: &xep0313; for history, &xep0421; for identity, &xep0503; for the channel list, &xep0488; for invitation links, &xep0513; for mentions, &xep0424; and &xep0425; for retraction and moderation.

This document is a framework. It defines the entities and the least a client and a service need to share to interoperate, and leaves channel kinds other than text, end-to-end encryption, content filtering and the service's operation to companion documents. It is a successor proposal that adopts the points the XSF's "GC3" discussions agreed on (membership apart from presence, sending without a session, explicit creation, stable occupant identity, tokens for invitations) and the requirements of the "New MUC" proposal; it is a fork of neither. It is unrelated to &xep0451;, which multiplexes connections between servers and holds the shortname mux; the registrar names here are therefore mux-chat.

ul.li: Membership is persistent and independent of presence; a member receives what it asked for at its bare JID while it has no session.
A room may hold several channels of several kinds; who sees and does what is decided per channel.
Roles are ordered and carry explicit permissions; an actor never acts on a peer or a superior.
Every text channel is a XEP-0045 room to a client that knows nothing of this document.
Discovery looks like a MUC service's, so room directories and client browsers work unchanged.
Rooms are created on purpose, never by a presence; an address is never reused.
Invitations are XMPP URIs any client can open.
Nothing is required of the participants' home servers.

section1.p: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in &rfc2119; and &rfc8174; when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

"The service" is the entity that implements this document at a domain; "a client" is any entity that talks to it. Where a rule is stated without a keyword it describes what the service does; such statements are normative for the service. Examples use the domain mux.example.org and the room verona; ids and tokens in examples are illustrative.

di.dd: The entity at a domain that hosts rooms, e.g. mux.example.org.
A bare JID at the service with members, hats, bans, invitations and channels. The room JID is also its first text channel, the lobby.
A bare JID at the service belonging to one room; it has a kind. This document defines the kind text.
A bare JID with a row in a room: an affiliation, a nick, hats and subscriptions. Membership ends by leaving, removal or ban, never by going offline.
A session admitted to a room without membership (Guests); it holds less than any member and leaves no row behind.
A full JID receiving live traffic from a channel, as a XEP-0045 occupant.
The &xep0421; identifier of a member, one per (member, room), the same in every channel of the room.
The member's name in the room, one per member, shared by all its devices and channels.
A &xep0317; hat as the room's role: a URI, a title, a position and a permission set.
A name from the catalogue of Hats and Permissions, either room-wide or per channel.
A channel's rule allowing or denying permissions to a hat or a member there.
How a stranger becomes a member: open, knock, invite or closed.
A &xep0488; invitation token issued by the room.

section1.p: An address is a slug: one to N characters of a-z, 0-9, _ and - after lower-casing, N being the service's slug-max-length (see the policy form). A room's slug is its localpart; a channel's localpart is the room slug, a dot and the channel slug. This is the service's convention. A client MUST NOT derive the room from a channel JID: the channel's disco#info names its room (Discovery). A service MAY give a room an opaque slug when the creator names none.

A slug once used MUST NOT be handed out again. A renamed channel's old JID answers every request with <redirect/> carrying xmpp:new@service?join; a destroyed channel's with <gone/> carrying its room's URI; a destroyed room's with an empty <gone/>. A presence to a JID with nothing behind it MUST be answered <item-not-found/>; it never creates anything.

section2.p: The service answers &xep0030; like a MUC service does. Its disco#info MUST carry an identity conference/text named after the service, the features urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0, http://jabber.org/protocol/disco#info, http://jabber.org/protocol/disco#items and http://jabber.org/protocol/commands, and a &xep0128; form of type urn:xmpp:mux-chat:policy:0 that says who may create rooms and on what terms. The feature urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#create MUST be present exactly when the requester may create a room now without a token, so a client knows whether to offer it.

section2.p: disco#items of the service lists every text channel, lobbies included, of every public room, as far as everyone may see it: one item per channel, named "Room · channel", each joinable as a MUC room. The node urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#rooms lists the public rooms. Channels of other kinds and channels not everyone may see MUST NOT be listed.

A room's disco#info is the lobby's (The XEP-0045 Face) plus the room's own: a second identity pubsub/service named after the room, the features urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0, urn:xmpp:spaces:0 and http://jabber.org/protocol/pubsub, a form urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#room and a form urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#channel describing the lobby.

section2.p: members counts the members (guests are not counted), online those with a session in any channel, channels the channels the requester may see; invite-create says who may issue invitations: admins, moderators, members or hats:URI; guests whether guests may join (Guests). disco#items of a room with no node is empty, as &xep0045; has it; the node urn:xmpp:spaces:0 is the channel list (below).

A channel's disco#info carries one identity by its kind (conference/text for a text channel) named "Room · channel", the features urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0 and urn:xmpp:spaces:0, a &xep0503; form whose parent is the room's channel node, and the form urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#channel. A text channel adds the MUC face's identity, features and muc#roominfo form, whose muc#roomconfig_pubsub field names the same node.

section2.p: A channel the requester may not see, and every channel of a private room to a JID that is not its member, MUST answer <item-not-found/>, as a channel that does not exist would.

The room JID is a &xep0060; service for one node, urn:xmpp:spaces:0, laid out as &xep0503; prescribes: one item per channel the requester may see, its id the channel's JID, its payload a &xep0402; <conference/> whose <extensions/> carry a <channel/> element of this namespace with the channel's kind, position and category, and, for a channel with requirements, a <requires> child with one <feature var='…'/> per feature var. The lobby's bookmark says autojoin='true'.

section2.p: Members are subscribed to the node by being members; anyone who may see the room MAY subscribe. A channel created, changed or renamed is an item notification, one destroyed or hidden from the recipient a retraction, sent as type='headline' messages to the bare JIDs of those who see it. Items are paged by &xep0059; or max_items. Publishing by clients is <forbidden/> with <publisher-not-allowed/>; the node configuration is read-only. A private room's node answers <not-allowed/> with <closed-node/> to a JID that is not a member.

A room is created at the service by an IQ carrying a submitted form of type urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#roomconfig, or by the &xep0050; command urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#create whose first stage offers the same form and whose result is a form of type urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#created with the fields room (jid-single) and channels (jid-multi). A service MUST support both. Either way the creator becomes the room's owner, with its localpart as nick.

<iq type='result' from='mux.example.org' to='romeo@example.org/orchard' id='c1'> <created xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0' room='verona@mux.example.org'> <channel jid='verona@mux.example.org' kind='text' name='general'/> <channel jid='verona.random@mux.example.org' kind='text' name='random'/> <channel jid='verona.voice@mux.example.org' kind='voice' name='Voice'/> </created> </iq>

section2.p: Errors: <conflict/> (the address is or was in use), <jid-malformed/> (not a slug), <bad-request/> (a value out of range), <not-allowed/> (the policy does not admit the requester), <not-authorized/> (a wrong creation token), <resource-constraint/> (at max-rooms-per-user), <policy-violation/> (the rules not accepted). A requester without a localpart MUST NOT be allowed to create.

A channel is created at the room JID by a member holding manage-channels, with <create-channel/> carrying a submitted form of type urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#channelconfig, or by the command urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#create-channel. The fields are slug (required), name, kind (default text), privacy (default inherit), hats (the hat URIs privacy hats opens the channel to), category, position (default: after the last), history, history-days and requires; a kind defined elsewhere adds its own. The answer is <created/> with the one channel.

section2.p: A requires value the service cannot enforce is <bad-request/>.

<update/> with a submitted form changes settings. To the room JID it takes a #roomconfig form with the room's settings: name, description, public, join-model, invite-create, guests (manage-room needed; setting guests to 0 removes the guests present), and the lobby's channel settings. To a channel JID it takes a #channelconfig form with the channel's: channel-name, position, category, privacy with hats, history, history-days, requires, and slug for a rename (manage-channels needed). A requirement added to a channel ends the sessions that lack it. A form naming nothing is <bad-request/>. The command urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#update offers the current values.

<destroy/> with an optional <reason/> to a channel removes it (manage-channels); to the room JID it destroys the room with every channel (owners only). The command urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#delete asks for confirmation first. Sessions in a destroyed text channel receive the XEP-0045 <destroy/> presence.

section2.p: A token (Invitations) admits under every model but a ban. A member already is one: its join takes the subscriptions it asks for and uses no token.

A client joins the room, not a channel, by an IQ to the room JID. It MAY name a nick (&xep0172;), a token, the channels it wants delivered to its bare JID (Subscriptions) and its entity capabilities (Channel requirements). The result carries the nick the service kept, the occupant id, the member's permissions in the lobby (Hats and Permissions), its subscriptions and, per subscribed channel, the archive's &xep0313; <metadata/> so the client knows where to catch up from.
section2.example:
<iq type='set' to='verona@mux.example.org' id='j1'> <join xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0'> <nick xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/nick'>Juliet</nick> <token>Zk3vQm9xT1bR4yW8nA2cEg</token> <subscribe channel='verona.balcony@mux.example.org' level='mentions'/> </join> </iq>
<iq type='result' from='verona@mux.example.org' to='juliet@example.org/balcony' id='j1'> <joined xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0'> <nick xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/nick'>Juliet</nick> <occupant-id xmlns='urn:xmpp:occupant-id:0' id='dd72603dXh3o6qK2pL9sW1Yz'/> <permissions xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:perm:0' version='p-4' affiliation='member' allow='attach change-nick invite react read-history send send-polls view'/> <subscriptions> <subscription channel='verona@mux.example.org' level='all'/> <subscription channel='verona.balcony@mux.example.org' level='mentions'/> </subscriptions> <metadata xmlns='urn:xmpp:mam:2' channel='verona@mux.example.org'> <start id='28482-98726-73623' timestamp='2026-11-01T10:00:00Z'/> <end id='09af3-cc343-b409f' timestamp='2026-11-23T09:12:41Z'/> </metadata> <metadata xmlns='urn:xmpp:mam:2' channel='verona.balcony@mux.example.org'/> </joined> </iq>
section2.p: The service MUST check in this order and answer the first failure: the target (<item-not-found/> with <no-such-room xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0'/>; <gone/>; <redirect/>; a channel JID is <bad-request/>), elements only the service writes (<not-acceptable/>, see Business Rules), a ban of the JID or its domain (<forbidden/>, before any token), the token (Invitations), then the join model: open admits; knock files the request and answers <registration-required/> with <approval-required xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0'/>; invite and closed answer <not-authorized/>. A nick another member holds is <conflict/>; nicks are compared after Unicode normalization, case folding and white-space folding. Without a nick the service uses the JID's localpart. A nick that is no valid resourcepart is <not-acceptable/>. A service SHOULD bound the number of requests waiting per room and answer <resource-constraint/> beyond it.

A knock waits until a member who may invite decides, by the command urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#pending at the room JID: a form of type urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#pending with the list-multi fields approve and decline, whose options are the waiting JIDs labelled with the nick and reason asked for. An approved requester becomes a member; it is not told, and its next join is a member's. A XEP-0045 affiliation change to member for the JID approves it too.

A member who may not invite can still send a XEP-0045 mediated invitation. The service relays it and files a knock that waits for the invitee's own word: its join (native or on the MUC face, answered <registration-required/> whatever the join model), its jabber:iq:register submission, or <consent xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0'/> set to the room JID with an optional <nick/> and <reason/>. Only then do the approvers see it. A service MUST NOT put a JID before the approvers on a third party's word alone.
The join is archived in the lobby as a joined event (Membership events).

<leave xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0'/> set to the room JID ends the membership; the room's only owner gets <not-allowed/>. The member's row stays as a tombstone (occupant id to last nick) so history keeps its names.

A subscription is per member and channel, at one of four levels: all (every message, subject change, affiliation change and system event), mentions (only messages that mention the member), none, and presence (as all, with occupant presence for a client that wants a live occupant list). The lobby is subscribed all by a native join and none by a MUC join. <update-subscription/> with one or more <subscribe channel='…' level='…'/> children changes levels and answers the full <subscriptions/>. A channel of another room or one the member cannot see is <item-not-found/>. How a subscription is delivered is in Passive delivery.

A guest is a session admitted without membership, for a room that wants a link anyone can follow: a meeting, a public event. A client asks to be a guest by putting an empty <guest/> of this namespace in its <join/>. A service MAY also treat sessions it knows to be anonymous logins (SASL ANONYMOUS, &rfc4505;) as guests whatever their join says; how it knows is a deployment matter. A member's <guest/> is ignored.

example.caption: A visitor joins a meeting as a guest

ul.li: A guest enters a room whose guests setting is 1 (else <forbidden/>) with a token, or an open room without one; a knock room without a token is <not-allowed/> (guests do not knock; nothing is filed), invite and closed are <not-authorized/>. The ban, the nick and the token are checked as for anyone; a token's grant and hats are not taken.

A guest wears the built-in hat guest alone, with affiliation none; it MUST NOT be given an affiliation, another hat or the right to invite. On the XEP-0045 face it is role participant (visitor without send), affiliation none, and absent from the affiliation lists.

A guest is never a persistent member: its row goes at its <leave/>, at a removal or a ban, and once it is present nowhere in the room; a service SHOULD sweep guests that have been absent for a few minutes. Its subscriptions deliver nothing (its levels are kept at none); it reads no archive older than its join, whatever the channel's history.
<guest/> marks a guest in <joined/>, in its <participant/> entry and in its archived events, so clients can show it.

section2.p: Self-declaration is safe because the guest hat holds less than everyone in every scope and the evaluation keeps it so (Evaluation): a user who declares itself a guest only loses rights, and one that does not declare gets what any stranger with an account gets.
Every text channel is a &xep0045; room to any client. The service MUST implement the following of it; the rest of XEP-0045 it MAY implement and SHOULD NOT contradict.

ul.li: disco#info: identity conference/text whose name equals muc#roomconfig_roomname; the features http://jabber.org/protocol/muc, http://jabber.org/protocol/muc#stable_id, http://jabber.org/protocol/muc#self-ping-optimization, urn:xmpp:occupant-id:0, urn:xmpp:sid:0, urn:xmpp:mam:2, urn:xmpp:mam:2#extended, urn:xmpp:message-moderate:1, urn:xmpp:message-retract:1, urn:xmpp:message-retract:1#tombstone, urn:xmpp:muc:affiliations:1, urn:xmpp:hats:0, urn:xmpp:muc-token-invite:0, muc_persistent, muc_unsecured, and one of each pair muc_public/muc_hidden, muc_open/muc_membersonly, muc_moderated/muc_unmoderated, muc_semianonymous/muc_nonanonymous as the projection says; the muc#roominfo form; status code 104 on any change of it. Apart from muc#roominfo_occupants the answer MUST be the same for every requester, so caches by &xep0390; hold.

Join by presence to channel/nick: <history/> honoured, then the occupants' presences, the self-presence with status 110 (and 210 when the nick was rewritten to the member's), the history from the archive, the subject message even when empty, then live traffic. The client's presence id is echoed on the self-presence and on a join error. Error conditions are XEP-0045's, each with <x xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/muc'/> and by on the error.

A join by a non-member of an open room is the room join: the JID becomes a member and the joined event is archived. A join by a non-member of any other room is <registration-required/> in a knock room and <not-authorized/> otherwise, unless <password/> carries a live token, which is redeemed as in the native join (a guest's, as a guest). An unavailable presence ends the session, never the membership.

In a knock room the feature jabber:iq:register is advertised: get returns the muc#register form with muc#register_roomnick and muc#register_faqentry (the reason), a submission is the knock, <remove/> is the leave.

Every message, presence and archive result carries the sender's <occupant-id/>, every relayed message its <nick xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/nick'/> and a <stanza-id by='channel'/>; the client's id is kept.
muc#admin and muc#owner read and write the projection. &xep0410; is answered by the service. Only &xep0199; pings are forwarded to occupants.
The channel MUST NOT be created by presence, locked, password-protected as an access model, fully anonymous, publicly logged (status 170/171) or destroyed when empty.
A channel with requirements has no XEP-0045 face (below).

section2.p: The nick is room-wide: a MUC join under another nick is answered with the member's nick, and the self-presence SHOULD carry status 210; a MUC nick change changes the member's nick in every channel. Occupant presence is sent only for members with a session somewhere in the room; a service MAY send a legacy client a subset above a threshold it chooses. Members without a session do not appear as occupants but may post; their messages arrive from='channel/nick' with an <occupant-id/>, which every MAM-capable client renders already.

A channel declares what a client needs to take part: requires, a list of &xep0030; feature vars, in its urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#channel form, its creation and configuration forms and its item in the channel node. Absent or empty, the channel is a plain XEP-0045 channel any client may join. A channel with requirements has no XEP-0045 face: it MUST be absent from the service's disco#items, and a MUC join presence to it MUST be answered <not-acceptable/>. The first use is an end-to-end encrypted channel whose protocol a client must speak; the examples use the placeholder urn:xmpp:mls:1 for such a feature, which this document does not define.

The service reads a session's entity capabilities, &xep0115; or &xep0390;, from the <c/> element in the native <join/> or in the MUC join presence, resolves the hash by disco#info to the client once and caches the features by hash; a session that sent no <c/> is asked by disco#info once. A subscribe to, a message to, or a voice join of a channel the session cannot use MUST be refused <not-acceptable/> with a <requires/> listing the features it lacks and a text, per session: another device of the same member with the features is admitted. Reading the archive is not gated.

section2.p: <participants/> get to the room JID answers members who see the lobby with the member list, versioned and paged by &xep0059;. A page has at most 100 entries when the request names no <set/>. Attributes filter: online='1', hat='URI', query='prefix' (of the folded nick), since='version' (the current version answers an empty list). Entries are ordered by the highest hat position (guests last), then the nick, then the join order. A real JID MUST be given only to a requester holding view-jids. Each entry names the hats the member wears by assignment; the hats its affiliation implies are not repeated. A stranger to a public room reads its counts in disco, never who is in it.

example.caption: The first page of the member list

section2.p: <summary/> get to the room JID answers a member with one <channel/> per text channel it may read: last is the newest archive id; for a channel the request named with since (an archive id), unread counts the messages after it not by the member and mentions those of them that mention it. One request replaces a MAM query per channel on reconnect. A service MAY cap the counts and the number of channels asked for.

section2.p: A member changes its nick room-wide by setting <nick xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/nick'> to the room JID: <forbidden/> when not a member, <not-allowed/> without change-nick, <not-acceptable/> for a nick the service cannot carry, <conflict/> for another member's. The change is a nick event in the lobby and a status 303 presence in every channel where the member has a session.

A member's standing is its XEP-0045 affiliation (owner, admin, member, none, outcast) and the hats it wears. Each affiliation implies a built-in hat and those below it; a hat may also be given by hand. A hat is a &xep0317; hat with a position and a permission set; the room's permissions in a channel are the union of the worn hats' sets, then the channel's overwrites. Permissions never travel in the <hats/> element itself, which stays as XEP-0317 defines it.

section2.p: A room keeps its own copy of the built-ins and MAY tune their sets; it MUST NOT destroy them, and of them only moderator is given by hand. A custom hat's URI is minted by the service under a prefix it owns unless the creator supplies an absolute URI outside the service's prefix; a URI never changes, so overwrites and mentions survive a rename. The hat's title is what XEP-0317 shows.

An overwrite belongs to a channel and names a hat or a member JID, a set of allowed and a set of denied permissions, and optionally an expiry (until, &xep0082;). A channel's privacy is expressed by overwrites: hats is a deny of view to everyone and an allow to each named hat; explicit the deny alone.

section2.p: The catalogue is readable on the wire so a client can label a permission it does not know: <catalogue xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:perm:0'/> get to the service, a room or a channel answers one <permission id='send' scope='channel' kinds='text'><label xml:lang='en'>Send messages</label></permission> per permission; scope is room or channel. How a timeout is placed, what pin, send-polls and bypass-slow-mode gate and what view-audit-log opens are left to the documents that define those features; the names are reserved here so hats carry them from the start.
For a member in a channel, the service MUST compute the effective set as follows.

ol.li: An outcast, or a JID under an unexpired ban: nothing. An owner, or a member whose hats give administrator: every permission of the scope.
The base is the union of the sets of every hat worn.

The channel's live overwrites apply in this order: everyone's deny, everyone's allow, the union of the worn hats' denies, the union of their allows, the member's own deny, the member's own allow. For a guest, everyone's allow is skipped. Room-scope permissions are left as they are; unknown names are ignored.
An active timeout keeps only view and read-history.
Without view, nothing at all in that channel. Without send, no attach, send-polls, mention-everyone or mention-groups. Without connect, none of the voice permissions.
The result keeps the room-scope permissions and the channel kind's.

section2.p: At room scope (no channel) steps 3 and 5's view rule do not apply. The order of step 3 means a union of roles, so reordering hats never silently changes rights, and a hat can open a channel that everyone is denied.

Hierarchy. An actor MUST be allowed to kick, ban, time out, overwrite or give hats only to a member whose highest hat position is strictly lower than its own; equal is refused, so an owner never acts on another owner. It creates, destroys and gives only hats positioned below its own, and grants (in a hat or an overwrite) only permissions it holds itself: room-wide for a hat, in that channel for an overwrite. Nobody but an owner grants itself anything. Only owners and holders of administrator pass step 1 untouched: an owner's overwrite binds admins.

Own permissions. <permissions xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:perm:0'/> get to a room or channel the requester sees answers its effective set there, as in <joined/>: version changes on every hat, overwrite, privacy or affiliation change of the room; allow is the space-separated set; affiliation the requester's (none for a stranger reading a public room, and for a guest); until the end of a timeout; each <hat/> child a hat worn by assignment. The element is the requester's own standing, which disco#info, identical for everyone, cannot carry.

Overwrites. <overwrites/> get to a channel JID (manage-channels or manage-hats) lists the channel's overwrites with the room's permission version. A set (manage-channels) replaces the entries it names (an entry with empty allow and deny removes one) and answers the new list. A version that is not the current one is <conflict/>; an entry naming both or neither of hat and jid, an unknown permission, or one both allowed and denied is <bad-request/>; a target at or above the actor, a permission it lacks in the channel, or an allow for itself is <forbidden/>.

section2.p: Hats. The six &xep0317; commands at the room JID (urn:xmpp:hats:commands:create, destroy, list, assign, unassign, list-assigned) manage hats; they need manage-hats and the hierarchy. create takes, beside XEP-0317's hats#title, hats#uri and hats#hue, the fields mux#hat_permissions (list-multi), mux#hat_position, mux#hat_mentionable and mux#hat_hoist; without them a hat has no permissions, position 1, and is neither mentionable nor hoisted. A plain XEP-0317 client works unchanged. create completes with a result form whose hats#uri is the hat's URI. list reports mux#hat_position and mux#hat_permissions beside XEP-0317's columns. A service MAY put the permission version in the hats#hash field of muc#roominfo.

<iq type='set' to='verona@mux.example.org' id='h1'> <command xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/commands' node='urn:xmpp:hats:commands:create' sessionid='h-1'> <x xmlns='jabber:x:data' type='submit'> <field var='FORM_TYPE'><value>urn:xmpp:hats:commands</value></field> <field var='hats#title'><value>Nurse</value></field> <field var='mux#hat_permissions'><value>view</value><value>send</value><value>pin</value></field> <field var='mux#hat_position'><value>2000</value></field> <field var='mux#hat_mentionable'><value>1</value></field> </x> </command> </iq>

section2.p: Per channel the service shows a MUC client an affiliation and a role computed from the effective set: an owner is owner/moderator; an admin with view is admin/moderator; a member with manage-messages or kick there has its affiliation and the role moderator; with send, participant; with view but not send, visitor; without view it is not an occupant and the channel is hidden from it; an outcast is outcast. The channel's flags follow what everyone holds there: muc_moderated when everyone lacks send, muc_membersonly when everyone lacks view or the join model is not open, muc_nonanonymous when everyone has view-jids, muc#roomconfig_changesubject when everyone has change-topic, muc#roomconfig_allowpm from send-pm. Real JIDs are shown to holders of view-jids alone, never by role: a deviation from XEP-0045, where moderators see them.

muc#admin writes map back: role none ends the session in this channel (307); visitor and participant are a member overwrite denying or allowing send here; moderator gives the built-in moderator hat; affiliation outcast is a room ban, member a room membership (approving a knock), none a removal from the room; admin and owner are set by owners. Affiliation reads answer the room's lists; &xep0463; and the member list name JIDs only to view-jids holders. The muc#owner form exposes the subset with a mapping (roomname, roomdesc, publicroom, membersonly, moderatedroom, changesubject, allowpm, whois); every change re-sends the affected occupants' presence and bumps the permission version.

section1.p: Invitations are &xep0488; tokens with an extension element in this namespace. The link is an XMPP URI (&rfc5122;) that every client opens: xmpp:verona@mux.example.org?join;password=TOKEN. An invitation MUST be presented as this URI and nothing else; how a platform opens xmpp: URIs (a web client registered as the handler, for instance) is outside this document. A legacy client stores the token as a password, which is harmless, since a token admits each JID once.
section1.example:
<iq type='set' to='verona@mux.example.org' id='i1'> <request xmlns='urn:xmpp:muc-token-invite:0' delay='604800' counter='5'> <invite xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0' scope='verona.balcony@mux.example.org' grant='member' label='household'> <hat uri='https://mux.example.org/hats/3f2a9c1e7b4d8a60'/> </invite> </request> </iq>
<iq type='result' from='verona@mux.example.org' to='romeo@example.org/orchard' id='i1'> <token xmlns='urn:xmpp:muc-token-invite:0' delay='604800' counter='5' creator='romeo@example.org'>Zk3vQm9xT1bR4yW8nA2cEg<invite xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0' id='9c1e4b7a2d6f8e03' scope='verona.balcony@mux.example.org' grant='member' uses='0' label='household' expire='2026-11-30T12:00:00Z' uri='xmpp:verona@mux.example.org?join;password=Zk3vQm9xT1bR4yW8nA2cEg'/></token> </iq>
section1.p: The requester needs invite and the room's invite-create rule. scope names the room or one channel the issuer sees; a channel-scoped token also opens that channel to the new member. grant is member, or admin from an owner. Each <hat/> is one the issuer could give (Hierarchy). delay and counter are clamped to the policy's bounds. The service MUST store only a hash of the token, with its id, scope, grant, hats, label, creator, expiry, uses and redeemers; the token text SHOULD be at least 128 bits of randomness (22 characters of base64url) and MUST appear only once, in this result. A service SHOULD bound the live invitations one member holds per room.

<tokens xmlns='urn:xmpp:muc-token-invite:0'/> get lists the requester's live tokens (an admin's: all) without their text, each <invite/> with its id and uses. <revoke/> set carries the token text or an <invite xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0' id='…'/> child, by the creator or an admin. An invitation dies with its creator's standing: when the creator leaves, is removed or banned, or may no longer invite, its tokens MUST be revoked. At redemption the creator's standing is read again; hats it could no longer give are left off and admin from a creator no longer owner is member.

Redemption, inside <join/> or a MUC join's <password/>: a ban wins; a member's token is ignored and not used up; a known token that is expired, used up, revoked or already used by this JID is <not-authorized/> with <expired-token xmlns='urn:xmpp:muc-token-invite:0'/>; an unknown one <not-authorized/>. Use and redeemer MUST be recorded atomically, once per JID. The joined event names the inviter's occupant id in <invited-by/>.

<preview xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0'><token>…</token></preview> get to the room JID, by anyone, answers a form of type urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#room-info with name, description, avatar (the &xep0084; hash), members, online, guests (whether guests may join), inviter (a nick), scope and expire, so a client shows the card before joining. The command urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0#invite (fields lifetime, uses, label) gives a generic client the same, answering the &xep0401; form urn:xmpp:invite#invitation with uri and expire. Previews and redemptions MUST be rate-limited per JID and per domain (<resource-constraint/>).

section2.p: Messages are type='groupchat' to the channel JID and are archived by &xep0313; on the channel JID, with urn:xmpp:mam:2#extended. The service rewrites from to channel/nick, keeps the client's id, adds <stanza-id by='channel'/> (&xep0359;; a foreign one with the channel's by is stripped), <occupant-id/> and <nick/>, and reflects the message to the sender. A member without a session MAY post. The payload picks the permission: a body needs send; a file share attach; a bodiless <reactions/> react; a <subject/> change-topic; a correction the author's occupant id; chat states and markers need view alone.

Mentions are &xep0513; markup; the targets are occupant ids, so they resolve in every channel of the room. Mentioning the channel needs mention-everyone; mentioning a hat or an affiliation needs mention-groups; a mention the author may not make is stripped and the message relayed, since refusing confuses clients that insert markup on their own.

Retraction is &xep0424;, by the author's occupant id; moderation is &xep0425; by a holder of manage-messages who outranks the author. Both leave a tombstone in the archive with the original's id, as those documents require; the moderation message itself is archived; nothing is deleted. Membership changes are archived events (below), so a client rebuilds the room's state from MAM alone.

A join, a leave and a nick change are archived in the lobby as groupchat messages from room/nick carrying <event xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0' type='joined'/>, type='left' or type='nick', with the member's <nick/>, <occupant-id/>, <stanza-id/> and a &xep0334; <store/> hint. A joined event names the inviter or approver in <invited-by occupant-id='…'/>; a nick event carries <previous> with the old nick; a guest's event carries <guest/>. They are delivered to sessions and subscribers as every other message.
section2.example: <message type='groupchat' from='verona@mux.example.org/Juliet' id='7c0e5f2a9b1d4e83a6f72c01'> <event xmlns='urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0' type='joined'> <invited-by occupant-id='a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2'/> </event> <nick xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/nick'>Juliet</nick> <occupant-id xmlns='urn:xmpp:occupant-id:0' id='dd72603dXh3o6qK2pL9sW1Yz'/> <stanza-id xmlns='urn:xmpp:sid:0' id='7c0e5f2a9b1d4e83a6f72c01' by='verona@mux.example.org'/> <store xmlns='urn:xmpp:hints'/> </message>

section2.p: A member with no session in a channel receives what its subscription level says at its bare JID, as a normal message from the channel that any &rfc6121; server routes, stores offline and pushes. The wire is the MUC subscription protocol of the ejabberd server (urn:xmpp:mucsub:0, documented at docs.ejabberd.im), restated here as far as this document uses it, so that a reader needs nothing else.

ul.li: <subscribe xmlns='urn:xmpp:mucsub:0' nick='…'/> set to a channel with one or more <event node='…'/> children subscribes; naming the node urn:xmpp:mucsub:nodes:messages is the level all and is answered with the nodes …:messages, …:subject, …:affiliations and …:system; naming none of them is none. A non-member is admitted as a MUC join would admit it. <unsubscribe/> is the level none. <subscriptions/> get to the service lists the requester's channels; to a channel, its subscribers, to moderators. The native <subscribe level/> sets the same level.

At all each message arrives wrapped: a <message/> from the channel to the bare JID carrying a &xep0060; <event/> with <items node='urn:xmpp:mucsub:nodes:messages'/> and one <item/>, whose id is the stanza id, holding the groupchat message as relayed. A subject change is an item of the subject node, an affiliation change a muc#user item of the affiliations node, an archived event an item of the system node.
A message that mentions the member arrives instead as a &xep0452; forward (<mentions xmlns='urn:xmpp:mmn:0'/>), at all and at mentions alike, so a push module recognises a mention without room state.
Chat states and markers are never delivered passively. Delivery goes to every resource without a session in the channel, not only when the whole account is absent.

ul.li: The sender of every request is the bare JID of its from. The service MUST NOT take anything else a client sends as identity and MUST refuse with <not-acceptable/>, on both faces, a client-sent <occupant-id/>, <hats/>, <stanza-id/> with the channel's by, any element of this document's namespaces it writes itself (<event/>, <invited-by/>, <previous/>, <permissions/>), a passive-delivery or XEP-0452 wrapper, a tombstone, a <moderated/> element, or a <subject/> beside a body. Nothing of a refused message is archived.

The occupant id is one per (member, room) and the same in every channel, because the room is the privacy boundary and mentions by occupant id must work across channels. &xep0421; recommends an id per room of a service; this document keeps that and adds that channels of one room share it. Ids MUST be unlinkable across rooms.
A room is created only by <create/> or the command; a presence to an unknown address MUST answer <item-not-found/> and SHOULD say in its text how rooms are created.

A private room MUST look like no room to a JID that is not its member: <item-not-found/> for every request but a join, a token preview, the registration form and a passive-delivery subscribe, and its commands are not listed to it.
Until its state is loaded a service MUST answer every request with a type wait error, never <item-not-found/>, so clients do not drop bookmarks.
The service bounds every text it stores (nick, name, description, category, reason, label, title) and MUST refuse longer values rather than truncate.
Membership, hats, overwrites, bans, invitations, subscriptions and the archive MUST be durable; a restart loses sessions only.

Entity capabilities are self-declared. The requirements gate keeps a client out of a channel it cannot use; it is a compatibility measure, not a security boundary, and the protocol a channel requires MUST make its own guarantees.
A client MUST NOT rely on the structure of JIDs: the room of a channel, the kind of a channel and the channels of a room come from discovery and the channel node.

section1.p: The reference implementation speaks this wire with the namespaces https://ns.another.im/mux/0, https://ns.another.im/mux/perm/0 and https://ns.another.im/mux/policy/0 in place of urn:xmpp:mux-chat:0, urn:xmpp:mux-chat:perm:0 and urn:xmpp:mux-chat:policy:0, the built-in hats under https://ns.another.im/mux/hat/ in place of urn:xmpp:mux-chat:hat:, and every #fragment form type and command node under those, until this document is accepted. The two are the same wire; only the namespace strings differ.

A service MAY derive the occupant id as the first 24 characters of base64url(HMAC-SHA256(key, room-id || 0x00 || bare-jid)) under a key of its own, which gives one id per (member, room) with no table.

A service MAY keep a hidden text channel per room as its moderation log, visible to the moderator hat; its format is not part of this document. Features of the catalogue whose wire is defined elsewhere (timeouts, slow mode, pins, polls) are evaluated by the permission algorithm here and placed by their own documents.
Clients that cache disco#info by &xep0390; rely on the answer being the same for everyone; the per-requester part of a member's standing is therefore in <permissions/>, not in disco.

Names, descriptions, categories and hat titles are free text in any script. Nicks are compared after NFC normalization and case folding, and MUST be valid resourceparts under &rfc7622;. Catalogue labels carry xml:lang. Slugs are ASCII by definition and are addresses, not names.

ul.li: The service stamps identity; it trusts no client-asserted element (Business Rules). Occupant ids MUST be unlinkable across rooms.
Real JIDs reach only holders of view-jids, in presence, affiliation lists, the member list and hat listings alike.

Tokens are stored hashed and compared in constant time; each admits a JID once; a ban beats a token; previews and redemptions are rate-limited per JID and domain. A token's power is the creator's at redemption, not at issue. The token is the invitation's whole secret and travels only in the xmpp: URI: a client SHOULD NOT write the URI into logs or hand it to a third-party service such as a link preview, and the service MUST NOT echo the token text after issuing it.
The hierarchy prevents escalation: nobody acts on a peer or a superior, grants what it lacks, or grants itself anything, owners excepted.

Guests are self-declared; this is safe only while the guest hat holds a subset of what everyone holds in every scope, which a room that tunes its built-in hats MUST keep. A ban of a guest whose JID is an anonymous login lasts for that login only; what keeps such guests out is the room's guests setting, its join model and a revoked invitation, and whatever the host server demands before an anonymous session (rate limits, a &xep0158; proof of work).

Knocks, invitations, previews, redemptions and nick changes are bounded per JID, per domain and per room; a service MUST answer <resource-constraint/> beyond its bounds rather than queue without limit.
Nothing a user wrote is deleted by moderation; tombstones keep the id. A service that drops rows after history-days does so by the owners' setting, which disco shows.
Operators of a host server MUST bind the service to its domain (the component's hosts); a component that may claim any domain can impersonate rooms.
A member reads in a channel only while it holds view there; hidden channels answer <item-not-found/> and are absent from the channel node, so their existence does not leak.

The requirements gate is not a security boundary (Business Rules): a client that misstates its capabilities is admitted to a channel it cannot use, and the protocol the channel requires must withstand that.

The service sees everything in a text channel: every message, who sent it, when, and who subscribed to what. End-to-end encryption is the business of the protocol a channel requires, not of this document.

Passive delivery puts the message, with the channel's and the sender's nick, in a normal message to the member's bare JID: the member's home server sees and stores it as it does any message, and a push service may see what the home server forwards.

A member list names members by occupant id and nick; the real JID is shown only to view-jids holders, and the lists a MUC client reads follow the same rule. Membership events in the archive name members by occupant id and nick, so a departed member's name stays readable but its JID is not revealed.

An occupant id is stable for as long as the membership and its tombstone last, so a member's messages in one room are linkable to each other, by design, and not to the same JID's messages in another room.
A token's redeemers are recorded, so the room's administrators learn which JID followed which invitation.
